intent: Make focus_owner's geofence trustworthy and self-explaining. It was failing in both directions: nothing blocked at home (a fuzzed coarse fix read as AWAY, restoring Firefox and so YouTube on the web) and everything blocked at the office (an empty last-known cache produced LOCATION_UNKNOWN, which applies the identical sweep to AT_HOME). Also unblock Play Store so inFakt can update, and allow Tachiyomi's per-source extension apks.
scope: NON-GOAL: making the DNS/VPN layer actually filter youtube.com (private_dns_host is empty; port 853 is not forwarded and VPN lockdown bypasses system Private DNS). A browser still reaches YouTube when AWAY.
changes: Declared and self-granted ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION via setPermissionGrantState (device owner needs no prompt); coarse is fuzzed to a ~1-2 km grid against a 150 m fence. Also self-grants coarse/background and calls setLocationEnabled(true), re-asserted every pass so a reinstall cannot silently drop them.

Replaced passive getLastKnownLocation with bounded active acquisition (20 s timeout) inside a location-typed foreground service, plus a LocationFix carrying age/accuracy/provider/outcome. Freshness window is 30 min - deliberately longer than the 15 min cadence, since a shorter window would mark the newest cache stale every pass and block everything.
A stale fix is now treated as no fix (fail-closed), which is only safe because active acquisition landed first.

Fixed hysteresis keyed off the wrong boolean: isEnforcing is true under AWAY too (YouTube stays hidden), so the threshold was permanently radius+hysteresis. Now keyed off a separate persisted was-inside-the-fence flag.
EnforcementDecision now reports distanceM, thresholdM, insideFence (nullable when unanswerable), curfewActive (from the clock, not inferred from the reason enum) and a per-package HideReason.

Added EnforcementLog: ring-buffered JSONL in filesDir read back over the platform channel, because run-as is refused on the release build and logcat rotates (measured empty while dumpsys showed 82 alarms fired). Records never contain coordinates.

New status card + debug log page: reason with a plain-English explanation, distance vs fence, fix age/provider/accuracy, curfew state, and every hidden app with the rule that hid it. LOCATION_UNKNOWN and no-home-set are rendered distinctly instead of reading as AT_HOME.

config.sh: com.android.vending added to WHITELIST (day only); new ALLOWED_PREFIXES/NIGHT_ALLOWED_PREFIXES seeded with eu.kanade.tachiyomi (day and night, per user decision), with prefix support added to both parsers and the exporter.

export.py: stopped subtracting the allowlist from blockable_system_packages. Sweepable is not hideable - removing an allowed FLAG_SYSTEM package from the sweep freezes it in its last state, which would have stranded Play Store hidden forever the moment it was allowlisted.
EnforcementScheduler now schedules the next curfew boundary; both callers invoked scheduleNext() bare, so the documented 23:00/05:00 exact alarms were never set and could land 15 min late.

Deleted lib/enforcement.dart and its test: a test-only second evaluator with no always-blocked concept, cited by KDoc as pinned by a PolicyParityTest that never existed. The UI now renders the Kotlin record instead of re-deciding.

Fixed a crash introduced mid-change: foregroundServiceType=location requires FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION; without it startForeground threw SecurityException on every alarm. Now declared, and the type degrades to specialUse if refused.

cachedFix now prefers the most ACCURATE cached fix, tie-broken by recency, instead of simply the newest. Newest-wins let a network fix accurate to a couple of km outrank a slightly older GPS fix, which cannot answer a 150 m question - observed on device as the reported distance swinging 763 m to 2.0 km while the phone sat still.

verification.evidence: 135 passed; focus_policy package at 100% branch coverage (model/loader/export/blocklist/__main__ all 100%).

BUILD SUCCESSFUL; EnforcementDecisionTest 25 tests, EnforcementLogTest 9 tests, 0 failures. Includes a test asserting no coordinate reaches the log record.

Everything is available except the always-blocked apps...' / Distance 763 m (fence 150 m) / Fix '3 min old · passive · ±100 m · cached_fresh' / Curfew inactive (23:00-05:00) / 3 hidden, 58 available; expanding shows youtube, youtube.music and chrome each as 'always blocked, everywhere'. Debug log page lists prior passes with timestamp, reason and distance.

risks: Active location acquisition costs battery each pass; bounded to 20 s and skipped entirely when a fix under 30 min old is already cached.

The 30 min freshness window means a genuinely stale fix can classify for up to that long. Chosen deliberately: a window under the 15 min cadence sends every pass of an idle phone to LOCATION_UNKNOWN, i.e. blocks everything.

Tachiyomi is now allowed during curfew (user decision 2026-08-14), which contradicts the previous night policy; the now-false prose in config.sh was updated in the same change so it cannot be 'fixed' back silently.
Prefix allowlisting is weaker than an exact list by construction - it permits packages that do not exist yet, so entries must stay vendor-specific.

Observed on device: the fix came from the 'passive' provider at ±100 m and distance jumped 763 m -> 2.0 km at rest. FINE is granted, but GPS indoors at the office is not resolving; worth re-checking fix.accuracy_m at home before trusting the 150 m fence.
rollback: git revert the commit; then regenerate the asset: python3 -m python_pkg.focus_policy --config phone_focus_mode/config.sh --output focus_owner/assets/policy.json --redact-home
Rebuild and 'adb install -r' the release APK. NEVER adb uninstall or pm clear - that strands device ownership with no holder and a factory reset becomes the only exit.
After rollback confirm: YouTube still absent from 'pm list packages -e', and the app still opens so the release-device-owner escape hatch stays reachable.
